sources.title: Planning application process
sources.verified_claim: Enfield reports 534 applications received in June 2026 with 87% registered within five working days; major applications target 13 weeks and EIA applications 16 weeks, subject to complexity and demand.

sources.title: Online planning searches
sources.verified_claim: Havering provides official searches for current and decided applications, decision conditions and appeals, giving a live traceability route without proving relevance to the sample parcel.

sources.title: Havering Infrastructure Planning
sources.verified_claim: Havering's Infrastructure Delivery Plan supports growth in the emerging Local Plan, identifies infrastructure gaps, costs and funding mechanisms, and is maintained as a live evolving document.

sources.title: Local Development Scheme
sources.verified_claim: Havering's current Local Development Scheme was approved in April 2025 and covers the 2025-2027 period, defining the planning documents the Council intends to prepare.

sources.title: Local Plan timetable
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's timetable schedules scoping consultation for 1 September to 9 October 2026, Gateway 1 for 31 October 2026, examination submission for 30 November 2028 and adoption for 30 April 2029.

sources.title: Evidence base
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's official evidence base explicitly separates housing, jobs, transport, environment, viability, infrastructure and neighbourhood evidence, supporting constraint/opportunity assessment but not exact parcel binding.

sources.title: New homes
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's New Homes Programme states a minimum target of 600 additional affordable homes on council-owned land by 2030, prioritising social rent and accelerated delivery.

sources.title: Infrastructure evidence
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's evidence page lists the Infrastructure Delivery Plan updated May 2020, so infrastructure context is retained with an explicit evidence-age limitation rather than treated as current parcel proof.
